info.title: Firewall Configuration API
info.description:
Programmatically manage and automate your Sophos Firewall — administration, authentication,
objects, networking, routing, sd-wan, wireless, vpn, rules, nat, traffic shaping,
active threat response, application control, intrusion prevention, tls inspection,
web protection, waf, malware and zero-day protection, synchronized security,
central management, logging, and monitoring — using the Firewall
Configuration REST API. This reference is generated from the official
OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the firewall appliance configuration.

### Base URL

All requests go to your firewall's configuration API host:

```
https://<firewall-hostname>:<port>/api/firewall-config/v1
```

### Authentication

The API uses token-based authentication. Send your API key as a bearer
token:

```
Authorization: Bearer <api-key>
```

Generate and manage API keys from
**Administration › API access** in the firewall web admin console.

### Naming and object references

SFOS control plane objects usually require a unique name to identify them
in POST requests. However, when GET|PATCH|DELETE APIs are performed on them,
they can be identified either by given unique name or an object ID (UUID).
Two custom formats define how these values are validated:

- `sfos-object-name` — an object name in valid UTF-8. No commas,
  semicolons, non-printable characters, or leading/trailing spaces, and it
  must never be a valid UUID.
- `sfos-object-name-or-id` — `sfos-object-name` **or** UUID.

Root **`updatedAt`** is when the document last changed (ISO 8601 UTC date-time).

name.description: Stable message identifier as a camelCase enum string (`MessageName` in OpenAPI; SFOS `messagekey` from `message_list`, 46 keys). Must be one of the declared enum literals, not a free-form string. See SCHEMA_README Message catalog (`name` → `group`).

updatedAt.description: When this singleton messages resource was last updated on the server (ISO 8601 UTC); applies to the document as a whole, not individual rows.

patch.description: Batch-update messages by `name` (each `name` must be a `MessageName` enum literal). Each `messages[]` entry updates or resets one message; an empty `message` resets that message to default. Messages not listed in the request are unchanged (not RFC 7396 full-array replacement). The `200` response returns the full document including root **`updatedAt`** when the singleton resource was last updated.

items.description: Application object definition. The same schema is used for GET and PATCH: properties that are server-controlled or immutable after create are marked `readOnly` (`id`, `name`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`). PATCH omits those fields and may include any subset of writable properties (`selectionMode`, `applicationFilters`, `applicationList`). The rows for applicationFilters use the same shape as application filter policy rule filters (`attribute`, `operator`, `values`). For smart search, use a filter row with attribute `smartFilter` and values that match expressions supported by the service. Successful GET and PATCH responses always include `id`, `name`, `selectionMode`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`. A `classification` filter always implicitly limits matching to cloud/SaaS applications. See the `classification` note on `ApplicationObjectFilter` for details.

As a result, a GET, POST, or PATCH response for an object with a `classification` filter may include an additional `characteristics` filter row with the value `Cloud Application`, even if the caller didn't specify that filter.

patch.description:
JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396). Omitted keys are unchanged. Nested `userInactivity` merges field-by-field; see
`StasSettingsUserInactivityUpdate` in the API specification.

schema.description:
Request body for updating tenant STAS (transparent authentication suite) settings (JSON Merge Patch). All
properties are optional. **`enabled`** and **`userInactivity`** are independent keys—you may send either, both,
or neither; they are not a `oneOf` (one does not replace the other). Omit `userInactivity` to leave the current
user inactivity policy unchanged. When present, `userInactivity` is merged recursively—use
`StasSettingsUserInactivityUpdate` (all sub-fields optional), not the full `StasSettingsUserInactivity` response
shape. This resource has no `name` field. For STAS VPN source networks, PATCH uses `StasVpnSourceNetworkUpdate`,
which omits immutable `name` and `id`.

enabled.description: Whether STAS is enabled.

restrictClientTrafficDuringProbe.description:
Whether to restrict client traffic during identity probe. Omitted keys in merge patch leave the stored value
unchanged; new or reset configuration defaults to `false` (see `StasSettings`).

userInactivity.description:
Partial user inactivity policy for STAS settings PATCH (JSON Merge Patch, RFC 7396). Every property is
optional; omitted keys leave the corresponding stored value unchanged. For example,
`{ "userInactivity": { "enabled": false } }` updates only `enabled` and preserves `inactivityTimeout` and
`dataTransferThreshold`. Omit `userInactivity` entirely to leave the whole policy unchanged.

enabled.description: Whether user inactivity handling is enabled.

inactivityTimeout.description: User inactivity timeout in minutes before the client is considered inactive.

dataTransferThreshold.description: Minimum data transfer volume in kilobytes that resets the inactivity timer.

fullUpdate.summary: Update several top-level fields and full user inactivity object

schema.description:

behavior, and user inactivity policy. Top-level **`enabled`** (STAS on/off) and **`userInactivity`** (nested
policy object) are separate required properties—they are not a `oneOf` alternative; both are always present in
the response body.

enabled.description: Whether STAS is enabled.

restrictClientTrafficDuringProbe.description: Whether to restrict client traffic during identity probe. Defaults to `false` when not configured.

userInactivity.description:
User inactivity policy for STAS client sessions, including enablement, timeout, and data transfer threshold.
Returned by GET/PATCH settings (`StasSettings`). For PATCH **request** bodies, nested updates use
`StasSettingsUserInactivityUpdate` (optional sub-fields, JSON Merge Patch) via `StasSettingsUpdate`, not this schema.

inactivityTimeout.description: User inactivity timeout in minutes before the client is considered inactive.

dataTransferThreshold.description: Minimum data transfer volume in kilobytes that resets the inactivity timer.

patch.description: Update the web authentication settings.

schema.description: Web authentication settings update request. Every field is optional; omitted properties retain their persisted values (RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch semantics). Cross-field rules are evaluated against the merged document; supplying openWebpageInNewWindow false together with logoutUserSetting closed is rejected with 400.

useKerberosForAdSso.description: Use Kerberos in addition to NTLM for Active Directory single sign-on.

displayCaptivePortalLink.description: Redirect unauthenticated users to the captive portal page.

displayUserPortalLink.description: Show the user portal link on the captive portal page.

useHttps.description: Serve the captive portal over HTTPS.

displayWebpage.description: Display a webpage to the user after captive portal sign-in. Gates openWebpageInNewWindow, redirectToRequestedUrl, and customUrl.

openWebpageInNewWindow.description: Open the post-sign-in webpage in a new browser window. Applied only when displayWebpage is true; if supplied while displayWebpage is false the value is accepted but not applied.

redirectToRequestedUrl.description: Redirect to the URL the user originally requested after sign-in. When false, redirect to customUrl. Applied only when displayWebpage is true; if supplied while displayWebpage is false the value is accepted but not applied.

customUrl.description: Custom URL to redirect to after sign-in. Applied only when displayWebpage is true and redirectToRequestedUrl is false. Syntactic URL validation is applied only when redirectToRequestedUrl is false; invalid URLs are rejected with 400 in that case. When redirectToRequestedUrl is true the value is stored without URL-format validation.

allOf.description: Trigger that logs the captive portal user out.

logoutUserSetting.description: Trigger that logs the captive portal user out.

dataTransferThreshold.description: Activity threshold in bytes used to determine whether a user is active. Applied only when logoutUserSetting is inactive; if supplied while logoutUserSetting is not inactive the value is accepted but not applied (the appliance normalizes the stored value to its default).

inactivityTimeout.description: Inactivity timeout in minutes after which the user is logged out. Applied only when logoutUserSetting is inactive; if supplied while logoutUserSetting is not inactive the value is accepted but not applied (the appliance stores an internal sentinel).

schema.description: Web authentication settings. The fields openWebpageInNewWindow, redirectToRequestedUrl, customUrl, dataTransferThreshold, and inactivityTimeout are always present in responses; their values are applied only when the gating field holds the qualifying value, otherwise the appliance ignores the stored value (the captive-portal UI hides the inapplicable controls).

redirectToRequestedUrl.description: Redirect to the URL the user originally requested after sign-in. When false, redirect to customUrl. Always present in responses; the value is applied only when displayWebpage is true.

customUrl.description: Custom URL to redirect to after sign-in. Always present in responses; the value is applied only when displayWebpage is true and redirectToRequestedUrl is false. inactivityTimeout.description: Inactivity timeout in minutes after which the user is logged out. Always present in responses; the value is applied only when logoutUserSetting is inactive. get.description: Get alert notification settings for this singleton resource. Each `notifications[]` row uses `name` and `group` as closed enum strings (`NotificationName`, `NotificationGroup` in OpenAPI), plus `displayName`, `email`, and `snmpTrap`. Root **`updatedAt`** is when the document last changed (ISO 8601 UTC date-time).

schema.description: Singleton alert notification settings document. Root **`updatedAt`** is when this resource last changed (any master switch or per-event row update). **`notifications[]`** rows include `name`, `group`, `displayName`, `email`, and `snmpTrap` only.

enableEmailNotifications.description: Master switch for email alert notifications.

enableSnmpTraps.description: Master switch for SNMP trap notifications.

items.description: Per-event channel toggles. `name` and `group` are closed enum strings (`NotificationName`, `NotificationGroup`); `displayName`, `email`, and `snmpTrap` are as documented. Root **`updatedAt`** on **NotificationSettings** reflects when this singleton resource last changed.

name.description: Stable notification identifier as a camelCase enum string (`NotificationName` in OpenAPI); must be one of the declared enum literals, not an arbitrary string.

group.description: UI grouping for the notification event. Enum values are fixed camelCase string literals per Sophos API conventions. The value `mdrNdrEssentialsXOpsAndThirdPartyThreatFeeds` is one logical group (maps to the combined MDR / NDR Essentials / X-Ops / third-party threat-feeds bucket in the product UI), not three separate groups.

snmpTrap.description: SNMP trap channel for this event.

updatedAt.description: When this singleton notification settings resource was last updated on the server (ISO 8601 UTC); applies to the document as a whole, not individual `notifications[]` rows.

AllEnabled.summary: Alert notifications with all channels enabled.

EmailOnly.summary: Alert notifications with email enabled only.

AllDisabled.summary: Alert notifications with all channels disabled.

patch.description: Partial update with `Content-Type: application/json`. Root booleans follow JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396): omitted roots are unchanged.       When `notifications` is present, each element requires `name` and may include optional `email` and/or `snmpTrap` (not `displayName`, `group`, or document `updatedAt`); the server applies catalog-keyed updates by `name`—not strict merge-patch whole-array replacement. The `200` response returns the full document including root **`updatedAt`** when the singleton resource was last updated.

requestBody.description: JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) for root booleans when omitted. When `notifications` is present, each array element requires `name` and may include optional `email` and/or `snmpTrap` (omit `displayName`, `group`, and document `updatedAt`); the server merges by `name`. Not whole-array merge-patch replacement.

schema.description: Partial update body (`Content-Type: application/json`). Include at least one of `enableEmailNotifications`, `enableSnmpTraps`, or `notifications` (servers may reject an empty object). Root booleans follow JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396): omitted roots are unchanged. When `notifications` is present, each array element is catalog-keyed by **`name`** (required); **`email`** and **`snmpTrap`** are optional per row. Only `name`, `email`, and `snmpTrap` may appear (`displayName` and `group` are not part of the PATCH body; root `updatedAt` is server-set on GET/PATCH `200` only). This is **not** RFC 7396 whole-array replacement and **not** an add/remove list wrapper. Omit `notifications` entirely to leave all per-event rows unchanged.

enableEmailNotifications.description: Master switch for email alert notifications.

enableSnmpTraps.description: Master switch for SNMP trap notifications.

notifications.description: Catalog-keyed updates: each item requires `name`; optional `email` and/or `snmpTrap` (not `displayName` or `group`; document `updatedAt` is not sent on PATCH). Not RFC 7396 whole-array replacement.

items.description: Per-event update row for PATCH. **`name`** is required to identify the catalog entry; **`email`** and **`snmpTrap`** are optional (include only the channels you want to change). `displayName` and `group` are returned on GET and PATCH `200` and are not accepted on PATCH request bodies. Root **`updatedAt`** on the document is server-set and not part of the PATCH body.

name.description: Stable notification identifier as a camelCase enum string (`NotificationName` in OpenAPI); must be one of the declared enum literals, not an arbitrary string.

email.description: Optional. Email channel for this event when present.

snmpTrap.description: Optional. SNMP trap channel for this event when present.

FullUpdate.summary: Update global toggles and selected notification entries (by name).

UpdateSpecificEvents.summary: Update only selected notification entries (no global toggles).

DisableAll.summary: Disable all channels and turn off selected entries.

schema.description:
Create an IPv4 multicast route.
Incoming and outgoing interfaces use objects with a required name field (object with name).
Source name can be a guest access point, a tunnel name (e.g. IPSec-VPN-1 or GRE), or a system interface (e.g. Port1). The default name "IPsec" is not allowed as the source name.
A client must not send source tunnel or destination tunnel types. These are managed by the server and not part of this API.
forwardToPbvpn is optional. When it's set, it controls IPsec or PBVPN forwarding and the server maps it to the outgoing interface configuration internally.

items.description: List of traffic shaping policies.
Traffic shaping bandwidth policy.

associatesWith.description: Target scope for the traffic shaping policy. Determines which type of network entity the bandwidth policy applies to.

isShared.description: Bandwidth allocation type. true: All matching targets share a single bandwidth pool. false: Each target gets its own bandwidth allocation.

type.description: Bandwidth policy type. guaranteed: traffic is guaranteed a minimum bandwidth and can burst up to the maximum. bestEffort: traffic is capped at the specified bandwidth with no minimum guarantee.

bandwidth.description: Bandwidth rate configuration. When the policy type is "guaranteed", provide the "guaranteed" object with min and max rates. When the policy type is "bestEffort", provide the "bestEffort" object with a single rate cap. Within each, use "aggregatedKbps" for a single combined limit, or "uploadKbps" and "downloadKbps" for per-direction limits. All rate values are in kbps (encoded in the field name). A future unit-aware sibling field (for example, "aggregated" as an object "{ bandwidth, unit }" or a quantity string like "10mbps") may be added later without breaking "aggregatedKbps".

guaranteed.description: Guaranteed bandwidth with minimum and maximum rates. min is the guaranteed floor; max is the burst ceiling and must be greater than or equal to min.

min.description:
Rate values in kbps (kilobits per second, 1 kbps = 1000 bits/sec).
Use "aggregatedKbps" for a single combined limit, or "uploadKbps" and "downloadKbps" for per-direction limits.

aggregatedKbps.description: Combined upload and download rate in kbps.

max.description:
Rate values in kbps (kilobits per second, 1 kbps = 1000 bits/sec).
Use "aggregatedKbps" for a single combined limit, or "uploadKbps" and "downloadKbps" for per-direction limits.

aggregatedKbps.description: Combined upload and download rate in kbps.

bestEffort.description:
Rate values in kbps (kilobits per second, 1 kbps = 1000 bits/sec).
Use "aggregatedKbps" for a single combined limit, or "uploadKbps" and "downloadKbps" for per-direction limits.

aggregatedKbps.description: Combined upload and download rate in kbps.

items.description: Schedule-based bandwidth override. Each override may independently use a different bandwidth type (guaranteed or bestEffort) and direction scope (aggregated vs per-direction) from the parent policy.

name.description: Schedule name (must match an existing schedule on the device).

bandwidth.description: Bandwidth rate configuration. When the policy type is "guaranteed", provide the "guaranteed" object with min and max rates. trafficShapingPolicy.description: Optional QoS / traffic-shaping policy applied when this category matches.

allOf.description:
Where the category's domain/keyword/URL data is sourced.
`local` means the lists are operator-managed via the
`domains`/`keywords` fields on this resource; `external` means
the lists are pulled from a remote URL given in
`externalUrls` and refreshed on a schedule. Use the documented
enum values to choose the appropriate source.

categorySource.description: Where the matching lists are sourced (local vs external feed).

domains.description:
Operator-managed list of domain patterns to match (used
when `categorySource: local`).  Each entry ≤ 250
characters; case-insensitive matching.

keywords.description:
Operator-managed list of keywords to match (used when
`categorySource: local`).  Each entry ≤ 250 characters.

externalUrls.description:
External feed URLs from which the category's domain /
keyword lists are fetched (used when

schema.description:
Web Scan Settings singleton — appliance-wide
controls for HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP scanning, PUA detection,
pharming protection, HTTPS decryption CA selection, and SSL
handling.  Operator-facing fields are grouped into two
cohesive envelopes (`malwareAndContent`, `httpsScanning`); the
only top-level operator field is the server-managed
`updatedAt` metadata.

malwareAndContent.description:
Antivirus and content-scanning controls applied to HTTP,
HTTPS, and FTP traffic by the web proxy.

allOf.description:
Antivirus scan engine selection.  `single` engages one
anti-virus engine (maximum performance); `dual` engages both
engines (maximum security) and requires Dual-AV licensing.
Requests sending `dual` on hardware/license that does not
support two engines are rejected with `400 badRequest`.

HTTP and HTTPS proxy traffic scanning mode.  `realTime` scans
content as it is transferred; `batch` buffers full objects
before scanning.

proxyScanMode.description: HTTP and HTTPS proxy traffic scanning mode.

maxHttpScanFileSizeKb.description:
Maximum HTTP and HTTPS file size eligible for scanning,
in KB.  Files larger than this value are not scanned.

maxFtpScanFileSizeKb.description:
Maximum FTP file size eligible for scanning, in KB.
Files larger than this value are not scanned.

bypassAudioVideoScan.description: When true, audio and video streams are not scanned by the web proxy.

allOf.description:
Action taken on content that cannot be scanned by the
antivirus engine (encrypted archives, oversize files,
malformed containers, etc.).  `block` denies the content
at the proxy; `allow` permits it to pass.  This is NOT
the action taken when malware is positively detected —
that is governed by `proxyScanMode` and the per-policy
action elsewhere.

malwareScanAction.description: Action taken on content that cannot be scanned by the antivirus engine.

blockPua.description: When true, potentially unwanted applications are blocked.

authorizedPua.description: List of PUA names exempt from PUA blocking.

pharmingProtection.description: When true, pharming protection is enabled.

httpsScanning.description:
HTTPS and SSL/TLS inspection controls — selects the
